newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Ratelindo to install 100,000 new lines.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Ratelindo to install 100,000 new lines.

text.p: Indonesia's fixed cellular telephone line provider Radio Telepon Indonesia (Ratelindo) said on Tuesday it planned to install 100,000 new lines this year as the company expanded services to West Java.

"We plan to install 100,000 lines this year. We also plan to expand our area into West Java, not just Jakarta," Nalin Rathod, Bakrie Brothers senior vice-president and chief financial officer, told reporters after a conference organised by PT ING Barings Indonesia.
Rathod said Ratelindo, a unit of Bakrie Brothers, had sold 75,000 lines by the end of 1996 and he was upbeat that the company would yield healthy profits this year.
Rathod, who gave no other details, said Ratelindo had a competitive advantage compared with the fixed telephone lines provided by state-controlled telecommunications company PT Telkom.
"The cost of building one line for Ratelindo is only around $500 which is much cheaper than the $1,400 required to build one fixed line," he said without elaborating.
Rathod said his firm would supplement Telkom in providing telephone services, especially to areas where the cost of providing fixed telephone lines was high.
